findings.title: Three Microsoft Defender Zero-Days Actively Exploited; Two Still Unpatched
findings.summary_md: Huntress told The Hacker News it observed in-the-wild use of BlueHammer, RedSun and UnDefend, three Microsoft Defender flaws released as zero-days by a researcher known as Chaotic Eclipse. BlueHammer, tracked as CVE-2026-33825, is a local privilege escalation flaw patched in the April 2026 Patch Tuesday update, while RedSun and UnDefend had no fix at publication and enable SYSTEM access and disruption of definition updates. Huntress said BlueHammer was weaponized from April 10, 2026 and proof of concept use of the other two appeared on April 16, after commands such as whoami /priv, cmdkey /list and net group.

findings.title: OAuth Device Code Phishing: 37x Surge in Enterprise ATO
findings.summary_md: The Cloud Security Alliance research note reported that Push Security documented a 37.5x increase in device code phishing pages by April 4, 2026, tied to the commercial launch of the EvilTokens phishing as a service kit on Telegram in mid-February. The technique abuses the OAuth 2.0 device authorization flow, so victims complete MFA on the real Microsoft login page and no password or session cookie is captured. The note says one EvilTokens campaign from February 19 through March 2026 affected more than 340 Microsoft 365 organizations, and that successful device code sign ins can be found in Microsoft Entra ID Sign-In Logs.

findings.title: Poisoning the well: AI supply chain attacks on Hugging Face and OpenClaw
findings.summary_md: Acronis Threat Research Unit reported active abuse of Hugging Face repositories and the ClawHub skill marketplace to deliver malware through AI ecosystems. It counted more than 575 malicious OpenClaw skills across 13 developer accounts, targeting Windows and macOS with trojans, cryptominers and the AMOS stealer. The trojanized skills instruct users to run encoded commands or install hidden dependencies, and hidden instructions use indirect prompt injection to make the agent act on behalf of the user.

findings.title: Prompts Become Shells: Semantic Kernel CVEs and Host-Level RCE
findings.summary_md: Infosec.ge analyzed Microsoft security research published on May 7, 2026 covering two Semantic Kernel flaws, CVE-2026-26030 and CVE-2026-25592, both scored 9.9. The Python Search Plugin passed model-controlled filter strings into an eval call behind an AST blocklist, and the researchers bypassed that blocklist to reach host command execution; semantic-kernel 1.39.4 replaces it with an allowlist. In the .NET SDK, DownloadFileAsync was mistakenly exposed as a kernel function, letting a prompt injection write a script to the Windows Startup folder on the host, and Semantic Kernel .NET 1.71.0 removes that attribute and adds path checks.

findings.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2026-42271 in BerriAI LiteLLM and CVE-2026-50751 in Check Point Security Gateway to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on June 8, 2026, citing evidence of active exploitation. The alert said these types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risk to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive 22-01 requires Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to remediate catalog entries by their due dates, and CISA urged all organizations to prioritize KEV remediation.

findings.title: LiteLLM Flaw CVE-2026-42271 Exploited in the Wild, Chains to Unauthenticated RCE
findings.summary_md: BerriAI told The Hacker News that the MCP preview endpoints POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list spawned a subprocess from a supplied server configuration with the proxy process privileges, protected only by a valid proxy API key. Affected LiteLLM versions run from 1.74.2 up to but not including 1.83.7, and the 1.83.7 release requires the PROXY_ADMIN role on both endpoints. Horizon3.ai chained the flaw with Starlette host header validation bypass CVE-2026-48710 to reach unauthenticated remote code execution, with Starlette 1.0.1 as the fixed version.

findings.title: One-Click Microsoft 365 Copilot Flaw Could Have Let Attackers Steal Emails, Files, and MFA Codes
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported that Varonis Threat Labs chained three bugs in Microsoft 365 Copilot Enterprise Search into a one-click exfiltration path named SearchLeak, tracked by Microsoft as CVE-2026-42824. The crafted link pointed at a real microsoft.com domain, so conventional URL filtering was unlikely to flag it, and the chain used a streaming render race plus a Bing image endpoint as an exfiltration proxy. Microsoft rated the issue critical and mitigated it on the backend, with CVSS scores of 6.5 from Microsoft and 7.5 from NVD; Varonis published a proof of concept, not observed exploitation.

findings.title: OpenClaw's Skill Marketplace and the Emerging AI Supply Chain Threat
findings.summary_md: Unit 42 analyzed OpenClaw skills distributed through ClawHub between February and May 2026 and found five malicious skills that remained unblocked after the marketplace integrated VirusTotal and ClawScan screening. Two delivered macOS infostealers with command and control infrastructure, one inflated its file size to exceed scanner thresholds, and two used agentic techniques for affiliate injection and front running. Unit 42 reported all five for takedown, and OpenClaw banned the accounts and deleted the skills.

findings.title: Statistical Report on Malware Targeting Windows Web Servers in Q2 2026
findings.summary_md: ASEC published its Q2 2026 review of attacks on poorly managed IIS and Apache Tomcat servers running on Windows, finding that intrusions typically started with web shell uploads followed by privilege escalation, reconnaissance, lateral movement and remote control. One case was attributed to UAT-8099 and used LockBit 3.0 ransomware alongside Potato, AnyDesk, GotoHTTP, LCX, the NPS client and BadIIS for control and SEO manipulation. The report recommends patching, stronger firewall access controls and updated antivirus software.
